title: Say "Maybe" to Your AI and It Hears "Do It."
summary: You float a half-formed idea to your AI the way you would to a colleague, and it does the thing before you've decided. The line between talking and doing has to be built in.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: You Trust Your AI Most on the Work You'll Check Least
summary: You check an AI hardest on work you could do yourself, and least on the work you handed off because you couldn't. The fix is an answer you can trace to its source in seconds.
author: Jack Raney

title: Your AI Stops the Moment the Answer Looks Finished
summary: Your AI aims for a reply that looks done. That only sometimes matches a task that is done, and the two come apart on exactly the boring jobs.
author: Jack Raney

title: You Asked for a Small Fix and Your AI Rewrote Everything Around It
summary: You ask your AI to change one line, and it also redoes four things you never mentioned. The model can't tell an edit from a rewrite, so the fix is telling it where the edit ends.
author: Jack Raney

title: Your AI Sounds the Same Whether It Knows or Guesses
summary: Your AI uses the same calm, fluent voice whether it knows the answer or is guessing. The tone can't tell you which you got, and an answer that points at its source can.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: The Best Reason to Run AI Locally Has Nothing to Do With Privacy
summary: Privacy is the reason I hear most for running AI on your own computer. I think access is the better one: an agent next to the files you give it takes on the small jobs that were never worth an upload.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: Your AI Agent Should Ask Before Anything It Can't Take Back
summary: An agent that never asks is fast right up to the mistake it can't undo. The interruptions worth having come just before a step that commits, like a reply going out or a calendar changing.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: Your Prompt Sets the Odds on What the AI Says Next
summary: Tiny prompt changes cause big swings because the model reads your words as the whole world and predicts from there. The mechanism explains the prompt tricks, and an agent you own lets you keep the phrasing that works.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: Your AI Should Not Disappear When Your Computer Does
summary: Your photos and files survive a broken computer. What your AI has learned about you should too. How Archie puts what your agent knows about you in one file you can keep somewhere safe and restore on your next computer.
author: Jack Raney

title: Why the Next Phase of AI Is Personal
summary: A year ago the big question about AI was which model is smartest. As every company gets access to capable models, raw intelligence matters less, and the useful AI is the one that knows you. Why I think the next phase of AI is personal.
author: Jack Raney

title: How My Agent Caught What a Silent Outage Left Behind
summary: A small complaint about a follow-up feature that never fired turned into a two-hour investigation with my coding agent. It found an expired credential, a hung background process, an appointment shown two hours off, and a date parser that had never worked.
author: Jack Raney

title: Why I Think AI Agents Are Underrated
summary: The reactions I hear most to AI agents are worry about jobs, or no thought at all. I think both miss what an agent is for: taking busywork off your plate and asking you at the step that commits.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: Why My Business Agent Drafted a Fake Client Plan
summary: My agent drafted a professional client email with a detailed action plan, and all of it was made up. The client's files never loaded, so the model filled the gaps with confidence, and the fix was in the setup.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: I Stopped Programming My Own Workouts, and My Agent Does It Now
summary: Every weekday, a custom agent Jack built for himself plans his workout from 60 days of training history, sleep, travel and his golf schedule. The session is on his phone before he's out of bed.
author: Jack Raney

title: How My Agent Caught What a Gmail Hacker Left Behind
summary: A call that showed Google's real phone number talked Jack into handing over his Gmail account. Less than an hour later, his AI agent helped him find hidden inbox filters, a planted passkey and a backdoor built to survive a password reset.
author: Jack Raney
